title: Mars in 3D
note: Real stereo pictures of Mars for red/cyan 3D glasses (red lens on the left eye). Every picture was taken by a machine on or above Mars and published as an anaglyph by NASA or ESA. Captions are short versions of the agencies' own descriptions. Sources and licences: CREDITS.md, written by tools/build.py.

chapters.line: The first rover on Mars, Sojourner, was the size of a microwave oven.

slides.title: Forward ramp and Twin Peaks
slides.caption: The lander's ramp, unrolled for Sojourner. Flat Top and Little Flat Top are at the centre, the Twin Peaks on the horizon.

slides.title: Sojourner's favourite rocks
slides.caption: Wedge at lower left; Shark, Half Dome and Pumpkin at the centre. The team named every rock.

slides.title: Yogi
slides.caption: A rock taller than the rover that drove up to it.

chapters.line: Built for 90 days on Mars. It worked for six years.

slides.title: Spirit's shadow
slides.caption: The rover's own shadow on the plain, with the Columbia Hills ahead.

slides.title: Larry's Lookout
slides.caption: A panorama from a spot the team called Larry's Lookout, on the climb up Husband Hill.

slides.title: West Valley
slides.caption: Looking west from the low plateau where Spirit spent the last months of 2007.

slides.title: Beside Home Plate
slides.caption: A 120-degree view to the south, after a short drive.

slides.title: A dust devil
slides.caption: West is at the centre, where a dust devil is crossing the plain in the distance.

chapters.line: Also built for 90 days. It drove 45 kilometres in fourteen years.

slides.title: Blueberries
slides.caption: Round grains a few millimetres across, nicknamed blueberries, on the floor of Eagle crater. They formed in water, long ago.

slides.title: Inside Endurance crater
slides.caption: A full circle around the rover, 11 metres inside the crater.

slides.title: Burns Cliff
slides.caption: The inner wall of Endurance crater, layer on layer, from its foot.

slides.title: Duck Bay, Victoria crater
slides.caption: Inside an alcove of Victoria crater, where Opportunity studied the rocks.

slides.title: Block Island
slides.caption: An iron-nickel meteorite, lying on the surface of Mars.

slides.title: Santa Maria crater
slides.caption: Opportunity's seventh anniversary on Mars. The crater is about as wide as a football field is long.

slides.title: Pillinger Point
slides.caption: A point on the western rim of Endeavour crater, with the crater beyond.

slides.title: Spirit of St. Louis crater
slides.caption: A rock spire in a shallow crater 34 metres long.

slides.title: Above Perseverance Valley
slides.caption: On the rim of Endeavour crater. A year later a planet-wide dust storm ended the mission.

chapters.line: A lander in the Martian arctic that dug down to ice.

slides.title: Snow White trench
slides.caption: A trench scraped by the lander's robotic arm.

slides.title: La Mancha trench
slides.caption: The depth of the trench, and the ice layer under the soil.

chapters.line: A rover the size of a car, climbing Mount Sharp.

slides.title: From John Klein to Mount Sharp
slides.caption: The rover's deck at its first drilling site, with Mount Sharp on the horizon.

slides.title: Hottah
slides.caption: Pebbles cemented into rock: evidence of a stream that once ran fast here.

slides.title: Dingo Gap
slides.caption: The full circle around the rover, on its way to a gap between dunes.

slides.title: Rock rows and Mount Sharp
slides.caption: Rows of rock at a spot called Junda, and Mount Sharp on the horizon.

slides.title: The Kimberley
slides.caption: Several kinds of rock at one waypoint, the day the rover arrived.

slides.title: Sol 1000
slides.caption: A full circle in a valley below Marias Pass, on the lower slopes of Mount Sharp.

slides.title: Namib Dune
slides.caption: The downwind face of a moving sand dune, four metres high: the first close look at an active dune on another planet.

slides.title: Funzie
slides.caption: Six and a half centimetres of rock, with hollows shaped like gypsum crystals.

chapters.line: A rover, and the first aircraft to fly on another planet.

slides.title: Ingenuity
slides.caption: The helicopter on the crater floor, seen by the rover's two Mastcam-Z cameras.

slides.title: Ingenuity flies
slides.caption: Its third flight, filmed by Perseverance.

slides.title: Raised Ridges, from the air
slides.caption: Two photos taken metres apart by the helicopter make the depth.

slides.title: Faillefeu, from the air
slides.caption: A mound the rover team was thinking of visiting, photographed twice from 5 metres apart.

chapters.place: Mars Express and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
chapters.line: One place photographed from two angles as the spacecraft passes over it.

slides.title: Noctis Labyrinthus
slides.caption: The Labyrinth of the Night, a maze of canyons at the head of Valles Marineris.

slides.title: Juventae Chasma
slides.caption: A deep basin north of Valles Marineris. North is to the left.

slides.title: Aram Chaos
slides.caption: Broken, jumbled ground inside an old crater.

slides.title: Eberswalde delta
slides.caption: River meanders in an old delta: water flowed here for a long time.

slides.title: Blade-like walls
slides.caption: Rock ridges as tall as a 16-storey building meet at angles and draw polygons.

slides.title: Victoria crater
slides.caption: The crater Opportunity drove to, seen from orbit: about 750 metres across.

slides.title: North polar ice cap
slides.caption: Part of the ice cap at the north pole. North is to the upper right.

slides.title: Phobos
slides.caption: The larger moon of Mars, about 22 kilometres across, photographed twice within ten minutes.

slides.title: The whole planet
slides.caption: The Rosetta probe flew past Mars on its way to a comet and took two pictures six minutes apart.
